title: Arguments from the command line
description:
Read options from `argv`.

```
$ ./calc add 3 4 5
12
$ ./calc max 3 9 4
9
$ ./calc
usage: calc add|max|min numbers...
```
hints: `char *end; long v = strtol(argv[i], &end, 10); if (*end != '\0' || end == argv[i]) ...` catches text that is not a number (lesson 3.05).
`argv[0]` is the program's name, so the numbers start at `argv[2]`.
requirements: The first argument picks the operation, the rest are numbers converted with `strtol`; a bad number prints `not a number: <text>`.
On the website, set the arguments in the Run options, or call a `run(int argc, char **argv)` with your own array.
stretch: Add `-v` anywhere in the arguments to print each step.
